PCI.BIO: Born in Bangladesh and joined Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission as Scientific Officer in 1977.  Went to Hungary and worked there under IAEA Fellowship program for one year (1980-81). Came to study at Marquette University, Wisconsin in 1981 and got MS in Physics with minor in Computer Science and another MS in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science August 1985.  In August 1985 I joined in the department of Physical Sciences at Texas Southmost College.  In August 1992 after merger, I joined in Computer Science Department at UTB.  In August 2015, I joined Computer Science Department at UTRGV. I live with my wife and two sons and have traveled extensively throughout the world.  I enjoy music, photography and travelling.
PCI.TEACHING_INTERESTS:
Game Development & Computer Graphics,
E-Commerce, Web Services and security
Web Programming and Development
Computer Networking and Database Programming
 and Computer Programming in C, C++, Java, Python, C#, F# & JavaScript

FACDEV.DESC:
	Attended a conference in the summer of ’97  (8th to 13th of August) titled Technology For Learning, held at UTSA – Academic Technology center.  I have also attended Pre-conference workshops which explore the following:
	Multimedia – introduces how to perform audio, video, and graphic capture and editing in hands-on approach.
	Instructional Design – explains how to use Designer’s Edge for instructional design for both in classroom and distance learning.
	Courseware Authoring – explores how to create multimedia instructional lesson inserting text, graphics, animations, video, and audio clips using Quest software.  The courseware titles are organized in layouts of frames and modules.
	Web page Construction – introduces basic structure and elements of Web page design.
	Distance Learning – explores the fundamentals of distance learning interactive sessions.

Students of this course are non computer science, hence
I preparing their mental process of how to solve a problem using pseudo code, flowchart, and hands-on activities. Reviewing chapter questions, and en course them to participate class discussion.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Multimedia Based Computer Assisted Learning Laboratory
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Through this grant, the development of a Multimedia-Based Computer- Assisted Learning Laboratory (MCALL) is used as a pilot project to improve the educational quality of undergraduates in science programs. The new lab can achieve the following educational objectives: (1) improve instruction and learning in biology, chemistry, physics, and computer science, (2) develop advanced skilled students in the area of multimedia, networking, and Graphical User Interface (GUI), and (3) train faculty to do computer-assisted teaching. The lab, MCALL, is being equipped with networked multimedia computer systems loaded with computer-assisted learning software. It serves a selective group of undergraduate students in biology, chemistry, physics, and computer science.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: An NSF Pilot Project on Student Retention
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the Frontiers In Education Conference ‘96
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper is based on a pilot project for which the funding was secured by The University of Texas at Brownsville from the National Science Foundation (NSF) under its Instrumentation and Laboratory Improvement (ILI) program. The proposal is to develop a multimedia based computer assisted learning lab (MCALL) to increase the present low student retention rate and enhance the quality of education in science and engineering technology for a predominantly minority student population. To achieve the objective, efforts will be focused on: improving the understanding of concepts in computer science, biology, chemistry, and physics through multimedia based interactive tutoring and experimentation; and developing technical skills for students in the area of multimedia, modeling and simulation.

PRESENT.TITLE: Internet Security and its impact on Online Education
PRESENT.ABSTRACT: This article presents an overview of internet security and how the security system impacts on the success of online education. The paper also reviews state of online learning and its future over traditional college and university based learning. It reviews the current state of internet security and explores different internet security threats and how it can be minimized. This article discusses different preventive strategies and techniques to protect internet servers and provide security to online education from such threats.
